default.why: A `persisted` write is on disk at a majority before the answer, which is Raft's own commit rule. On etcd's spec no committed entry was lost with crashes, a lost disk (E-14c) or one damaged replica under `rejoin` (E-37, 27,985 states). E-29's journal of the same shape lost 0 of 10,020 acknowledged batches in 2,640 LazyFS power cuts; the sweeps on the real kernel are phase 2.

PD.why: The commit rule is Raft's, but PD keeps Z `crash` and an LSM store. E-37 shows a committed write lost with one bad entry under `crash`, and no power-loss run covered its store.
PD.closes: a LazyFS run on its store and the sim's disk model; none is planned for this row

ISR.why: Its commit is the in-sync set under an outside controller. No experiment modelled that composition, so there is no lost-write check for it.
ISR.closes: a model of the in-sync set and controller rules with crashes and disk loss, then the 1,000-seed sim sweeps with crashes and power loss, and LazyFS on the real journal (phase 2)

SLOG.why: Its commit is a write quorum of log nodes, changed by a seal and a metadata CAS. That protocol was not modelled here (SPACE counts 3 to 4 novel mechanisms in it).
SLOG.closes: a model of the seal and CAS with crashes and disk loss, then the 1,000-seed sim sweeps with crashes and power loss, and LazyFS on the real journal (phase 2)

OBJ.why: An acknowledged write is a finished PUT, so the machines hold nothing that must survive. But the manifest CAS and the lease that order the PUTs were only timed (E-28), never modelled.
OBJ.closes: a model of the manifest CAS and writer lease

V4.why: v4's ledger lists a commit stranded on a cut-off owner (STATUS.md). Whether a `persisted` write can be lost by it was not run in this study.
V4.closes: v4's own sweeps with a lost-write monitor; not planned

BUY.why: JetStream with three file replicas and an fsync before the ack lost none of 900 writes through a leader kill (E-44). No power-loss or disk-loss run was made.
BUY.closes: a LazyFS and disk-loss run on JetStream; not planned

default.why: Each dedup option held ONCE and REFUSED in E-20's exhaustive model under lost answers, a failover and a move in mid-retry (`sess` 13 rules, 14 under `fwd`; `win` 17 and 19). Porcupine and Knossos pass on the prototype's histories with A-04's refusal wait, and A-05's marks keep derived outputs once past the horizon (E-30).

PD.why: Its dedup is transaction ids under two-phase commit. That is published (Percolator), but no experiment here modelled it.
PD.closes: a model of `txn` under `2pc`; none is planned

ISR.why: `pid` holds in E-20's model after A-22's two fixes, given one writer and a committed prefix across a failover. The in-sync-set failover that must give those was not modelled here.
ISR.closes: a model of the ISR leader change under E-20's scenarios

SLOG.why: `win` holds in E-20's model given one writer at a time. SLOG's writer change (seal and CAS) was not modelled, and a late append by the old writer is the case that matters.
SLOG.closes: a model of the seal and writer change under E-20's scenarios

OBJ.why: `sess` holds in E-20's model given one writer at a time. OBJ's writer change by a lease and a manifest CAS was not modelled.
OBJ.closes: a model of the lease and manifest CAS under E-20's scenarios

SIDE.why: E-20's rules hold for writes. But SIDE runs calls at the leader (U `ldr`), and a call in flight across a handover was never modelled; SPACE counts it as one novel rule.
SIDE.closes: an E-20-style model of calls in flight across a handover

V4.why: v4's own scoped sweep pins it (STATUS.md, KNOWN_UNSAFE, A2 seed 9). Step by step: a forwarded write commits at the owner; a cut strands that commit; the issuer retries; the new owner commits it again; both stand after the heal. A write issued from a tap is also committed twice.

BUY.why: Measured on JetStream: a retry lands twice once the dedup window has passed, and an `incr` retried after one other write to the row was counted again (3 where 2 was right). The attempt id lives only in the row's last message, and fero cannot change the log.

default.why: One leader per term is Raft's rule: with A-01's campaign guard no invariant broke on etcd's spec (E-14c), and the port was linearizable in 26 of 26 Maelstrom runs under partitions (E-46). A partition has one writing group at a time by the move's fence and open entries (E-15: TLC agrees on all 74 runs; E-17c for split and re-key). A cut-off member refuses at once with a redirect by A-02's rule, which is stated and not yet built.

RLOG.why: The log group is Raft, and its leader takes an append only with the latest committed writer epoch. E-16 model-checked the writer handover: 9 rules, all needed.

ISR.why: One writer rests on leader epochs and an outside controller (the KIP composition). None of it was modelled here.
ISR.closes: a model of the ISR and controller rules under partitions

SLOG.why: One writer rests on sealing a loglet and a metadata CAS. That protocol was not modelled here.
SLOG.closes: a model of the seal and CAS under partitions

OBJ.why: The writer holds a lease by CAS on the store's manifest, and reads use a time lease that needs bounded clock drift. Neither was modelled (E-28 timed the CAS only).
OBJ.closes: a model of the lease and manifest CAS

V4.why: Step by step: (1) v4 is leaderless, any replica takes writes and cells merge by last-writer-wins (SPACE R `lww`). (2) SPACE names writes on both sides of a split as what v4 keeps. (3) STATUS.md pins a commit made by a cut-off owner that the new owner then makes again. So two writers can commit to one partition at once, and a cut-off side does not refuse.

BUY.why: A stream has one Raft leader, and 60 lock acquires never overlapped through a leader kill (E-44). No partition run was made, and fencing is by convention.
BUY.closes: partition schedules against JetStream; not planned

Judged for the `persisted` rung.

BUY.why: Four patterns passed their checks through a leader kill (E-44), but no reader history was checked, and no partition or power-loss run was made.

Restated as C plus the normal gap plus 5 ms it is open: the port's handover was not timed, and failover at E = 2 s with 0.25 E jitter sums to 2.5 s with no margin (reasoned, not run).

SLOG.why: A writer change is a seal plus a metadata CAS plus a new writer. None of it was timed here.

default.why: From three voters up a Raft group has no stuck state with a live majority on etcd's spec (E-14b: 5,165,341 states, complete; E-14c with grow first). A-01's stated limit: while a group grows from two voters to three there is a one-message window in which it waits for its old leader, so the other two returning is not enough (model-checked, 6 and 4 stuck states). Read as a two-voter group's limit this is open until the harness runs; if F-07 counts the new voter from the commit, the window is a counterexample.

Step by step: each leaver's dir holds the view it saw last, one it is not in; so the first two back sit `joining` until the last returns; no kernel rule can re-form them safely. v4's own `stopsOneByOne` harness pins it on the sim and on real sockets, and the ledger marks it decided, not changed.

BUY.why: JetStream's Raft should return with any majority, but only a leader kill was run (E-44), not a full stop.
BUY.closes: a stop-all and restart-in-any-order run on JetStream; not planned

default.why: The kernel runs on a worker (M `kw`, A-27). Through a 5 s main-thread stall it kept its heartbeat within 5 ms and write p99 at or under 4 ms, where a main-thread kernel went silent for 2.6 to 5.1 s (E-07). A throw on the main thread cannot reach the kernel's thread; writer rules run on the kernel thread under a time budget, whose cost is a phase-2 pin.

SRV.why: No user code runs on the servers (U `cli`): apps are clients, and the native kernel has its own threads. So a throw or a stall in user code cannot reach replication.

PD.why: No user code runs on the servers (U `cli`): apps are clients of a native server. So a throw or a stall in user code cannot reach replication.

EMB-V8.why: User code runs in V8 isolates; the Rust kernel has its own threads, so a stalled or throwing isolate cannot hold them. E-07 measured the same split between two threads in Node.

SIDE.why: Replication and failure detection sit in the native daemon, so a stalled app cannot stop them. But L2 runs in the app's Node process for the groups its host leads, so whether writes go on through a 5 s stall there was not shown.
SIDE.closes: a SIDE prototype under a 5 s stall of the app process

V4.why: Step by step: (1) v4 runs kernel, fold and user code on one event loop (M `loop`). (2) A synchronous stall in user code blocks that loop, so the kernel sends no heartbeat and no acknowledgement. (3) E-07 measured it: a main-thread kernel went silent for 2.6 to 5.1 s in a 5 s stall, past any 2 s election time.

BUY.why: Replication and failure detection are in JetStream's own server processes. fero's code and the user's run in the client, so they cannot stall them.

default.why: Z `rejoin` (A-28): a checksum per entry turns damage into a wipe, and the wiped replica never votes under its old id. On etcd's spec with three voters and one damaged entry all 10 invariants hold and 0 of 1,178 judged states are stuck (27,985 states); without either rule a committed write is lost in 32 states. Whether one bad entry wipes one group or the whole journal is K-24.

PD.why: PD keeps Z `crash`: Raft as published, with no checksum per entry. TLC on etcd's spec: one voter cuts one bad entry as a torn tail, votes for a lagging candidate, and the new leader overwrites a committed write (one fault, 32 states). The fix is another row's option (`rejoin` or `par`).

ISR.why: Z `crash` and not Raft: SPACE calls a corrupt entry undefined for it, and E-37 did not check it. An in-sync leader that cuts a bad entry is the case to model.
ISR.closes: an E-37-style model of this family with one lost or corrupted entry

OBJ.why: Z `crash` and not Raft: E-37 did not check it. The log lives in the store, so a bad local entry is a cache fault, but no rule or run says what the server does with it.
OBJ.closes: an E-37-style model of this family with one lost or corrupted entry

SLOG.why: It takes A-28 by reasoning only: its data path is a write quorum of log nodes, not Raft, so E-37 did not check a damaged log node there.
SLOG.closes: an E-37-style model of this family with one lost or corrupted entry

V4.why: Z `crash`, and not checked here. v4 has no vote on data entries; what a damaged journal entry does to its lanes was not run.
V4.closes: an E-37-style model of this family with one lost or corrupted entry; not planned

BUY.why: The log and its checksums are JetStream's. No damaged-entry run was made on it.
BUY.closes: a damaged-entry run on JetStream; not planned

default.why: Z `rejoin` wipes each damaged replica, so one bad entry on each of two replicas is two lost voters of three: every such state is stuck without F-12's operator step (E-37, `rejoin2`). Only Z `par` keeps the group writable (0 of 276 two-damage states stuck), and no row holds it.

PD.why: Z `crash` finds no damage, so it has nothing to repair. It stays writable only by cutting the entries and losing committed writes (E-37, `cut`).

SLOG.why: Z `rejoin` by its own definition wipes both damaged log nodes, which loses the write quorum of three and needs F-12 (reasoned from SPACE and E-37; SLOG's path was not run).

ISR.why: Not checked: E-37 ran Raft only, and this row's storage-fault rule is undefined (Z `crash`) or not its own.

OBJ.why: Not checked: E-37 ran Raft only, and this row's storage-fault rule is undefined (Z `crash`) or not its own. A bad local entry could be read again from the store (reasoned).

V4.why: Not checked: E-37 ran Raft only, and this row's storage-fault rule is undefined (Z `crash`) or not its own. v4's digests could refill a lane from peers (reasoned).

BUY.why: Not run on JetStream; the repair, if any, is its own.
